title: Introduce privilege escrow proxy and jurisdictional audit fanout
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add a privilege escrow proxy to mediate operator-scoped elevated actions with jurisdiction-aware KMS consent; introduce audit fanout so audit records are routed to regional compliance sinks. Backwards-compatible rollout via shadow mode and canary. No customer-facing API changes.
description:
Context and motivation: Customers running Redwood Private and Dedicated deployments requested stronger operator-privilege controls, a way to timebox elevated actions, and deterministic audit delivery to jurisdiction-specific sinks. This PR implements a lightweight privilege-escrow proxy that mediates transient operator leases and ties KMS consent checks to jurisdictional assertions, and adds an audit fanout pipeline so a single operation can produce jurisdiction-aware audit envelopes for multiple compliance endpoints. Goals: 1) reduce blast radius of operator escalations, 2) ensure KMS key usage is region-asserted before decrypt/encrypt operations, 3) guarantee audit visibility across regional compliance sinks with deterministic delivery semantics.

What changed (high level): - New service: privilege-escrow-proxy (internal HTTP gRPC shim) that issues short-lived operator leases (JWT-like opaque tokens) after validating RBACv2 attribute assertions. Leases include jurisdiction pins and scope hashes. - KMS integration: escrow proxy invokes a KMS-consent-checker plugin before issuing a lease. The plugin verifies that requested key material is permitted in the claimed jurisdiction and produces a signed consent token attached to the lease. - Audit fanout: modified audit-writer to accept jurisdictional envelopes and fan them out to regional sinks (S3/GCS buckets, syslog endpoints, or webhook endpoints) with per-sink backpressure and retry; includes pluggable redaction rules per jurisdiction. - RBAC changes: small RBACv2 policy extension to include "escrow:request" action, attribute-based constraints (data_class, geo_zone), and operator approval traces. - Config and rollout: feature flag (priv-escrow.enabled) with three modes: shadow, enforced-canary (percentile by operator id), enforced-global. Default is shadow. - Observability: metrics for lease issuance latency, KMS consent failures, audit-fanout queue length, and per-jurisdiction delivery success rate.

Implementation notes: - The escrow proxy is implemented in Go and reuses existing operator-authn libraries; it signs leases with the cluster operator key and stores ephemeral lease metadata in the existing metadata-store with TTL. - KMS consent plugin is pluggable; currently implemented adapters for AWS KMS and GCP KMS using a consent cache with LRU eviction and TTL of 60s. Consent tokens are HMAC-signed and include the key id, jurisdiction, and a nonce to prevent replay. - Audit fanout extends audit-writer with per-sink delivery workers and a durable on-disk queue for Private installations (when remote sinks are unavailable the envelope is persisted encrypted to the local audit store). - Small RBACv2 policy compiler changes to allow a new attribute matcher syntax (geo_zone == "eu" or geo_zone in ["eu","uk"]). Compiler includes validation to prevent superset-downgrade (rejects policies that would widen operator scope when privilege-escrow.enabled == enforced-global).

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked: Linear ENG-4217 - [x] Unit tests for lease issuance and TTL logic - [x] Integration tests for KMS consent adapter (mocked KMS) - [x] E2E canary with shadow mode enabled by default - [x] Documentation: security-runbook and admin guide updated - [x] Backwards compatible: existing operator flows unchanged when feature flag is off

How this was tested: - Unit and integration tests in CI (see checks below). - Local end-to-end run against a dev cluster with a mocked KMS; exercised failover paths when KMS consent failed and verified audit envelopes persisted locally. - Canary: deployed to Dedicated staging region with 5% operator assignment and observed metrics for 48 hours. No production customer-facing errors reported. - Security review: two rounds of security review by SEC team (SEC-134) focusing on token signing and replay protections.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main in shadow mode. 2) Enable enforced-canary for a subset of operator IDs (2%) for one week and monitor: lease issuance errors, KMS consent failure, audit delivery latency. 3) Gradually increase canary to 25% then 75% if metrics stable. 4) Enforce globally after 7 days of stability. Rollback: toggle priv-escrow.enabled to off to return to legacy flows; audit fanout has an opt-out per deployment via priv-audit.fanout.enabled. Emergency hotfix path documented.

Backward compatibility & migration: - No changes to public API surface for customers. - Private installer will toggle a default config; upgrade notes added in docs/ops/privilege-escrow.md explaining how to configure jurisdictional sinks and KMS adapters.

Security considerations: - All lease tokens are short-lived (default 5m), signed with cluster operator key (rotation policy enforced), and include a nonce. - Consent tokens include nonces and HMAC signature; KMS adapters validate token freshness. - Audit envelope includes redaction hints and is encrypted on disk using the deployment CMK. - RBACv2 compiler rejects policies that would silently broaden operator privileges; admins must explicitly grant escrow request capability.

Related work and alternatives considered: - Considered extending existing operator-approval-queue but opted for separate proxy to keep attachment surface small and allow finer-grained jurisdiction pinning. - Considered using federated KMS proxy but current consent cache approach provides better latency for short-lived leases.

Notes: This PR focuses on correctness and traceability rather than micro-optimizations; follow-up work planned to add batching for KMS consent checks when multiple lease requests originate from the same operator during short time windows.
commits: 3 commits: 1) Add privilege-escrow-proxy service skeleton, CLI flags, and configuration docs; 2) Implement KMS consent adapter, consent cache, and unit tests; 3) Extend audit-writer with jurisdictional envelope support and durable queue; plus small RBACv2 compiler adjustments and docs updates.
review_comments: Omar Patel: Please ensure the consent cache has a defensible TTL and eviction policy; we should avoid false positives when KMS metadata lags (addressed in cache.go with 60s TTL and LRU limit).
Linnea Sørensen: Can we add an alarm for audit-fanout queue growth beyond 10k pending envelopes? Added metric + alert in observability metrics and docs.
Diego Alvarez: Confirmed HMAC secrets for consent tokens are rotated by ops; request added to runbook. Author responded: ops-runbook updated and rotation test added to CI.
SEC review (Anna Müller): Suggest adding replay-protection tests for consent tokens; added tests and strengthened nonce usage to include operator session id.
